"Who cares" they say, "we already got their pre order money." Then that retarded intern says, "Won't this hurt our reputation?" To which they reply, "Yeah, but we'll just come out with another game trailer next year and they'll do it all over again." Then they laugh and laugh. Or how about that DRM that straight up breaks the game, and locks the paying customers out, meanwhile the pirates have cracked that shit and can actually enjoy the damn thing. Then once everyone is utterly sick of it, they put it on hold until the next generation of gamers show up, then it starts over again. "We're not gonna send out review copies anymore, because we've learned people just buy our games." Or how about the fact that some companies believe that all those games you bought years ago don't matter, because fuck backwards compatibility. "Why the hell do you need that?", they say. We're gonna come out with a remastered version of that, it's better then the original one you bought. We upped the resolution and added original concept art, that's worth paying another 60 dollars right?

What about the companies, developers, and game journo's that treat gamers like utter garbage, calling them racist and sexist and call them entitled. Oh I'm sorry, I just dropped a good chunk of money for this thing, silly me for thinking I'm owed something. Not like all the aforementioned are in cahoots with one another, as we've seen before.

Or maybe the fact that parasites known as SJW's have infected every level of the gaming industry, and they justify it cause they want to "clean up the industry" until everyone feels included.... yuh know, except the people that built the thing in the first place. It's obvious that the majority of the industry has absolutely no respect for gamers... Don't get me wrong there are good companies out there that deserve respect and admiration, but they don't come along very often anymore. When they do they should be praised. But...

If any of these things are gonna change, we as a collective have to grow a spine. No more buying into any of this shit. Learn to hold on to your principles and go against the things that are bleeding you dry! And what so many people need to learn is, you don't have to consume what they feed you. You can skip that pre order, you don't need the expansion, hell let's just say it, you don't. need. that. game. I can already here people now, "I don't mind paying", "We should support developers so they don't go out of business", "But the game looks soooo good.", "I gotta, it's like, my favorite game." All excuses. It's these excuses that got us where we are now. And what these people need to understand is, for a little bit of discomfort now (because not buying a game is so terrible) the industry as a whole could change for the better, and in our favor. These companies will claw to survive, so we need to teach them they better start working for us then.

This doesn't mean you have to go without. If you miss that big game you wanted because of the way it decided to do business most people need to realize there will always be another game that comes along that takes it's place and learns from the mistake of the first one. Hell, the first one might go free to play if you wait a little bit. Support people that actually care. Indie devs and companies that give you a good value for your money. They exist, you just gotta watch for them.

If we stand together as gamers we can change this corrupted industry, we just have to be patient.

This is a good place to throw out a plug for "Darkwood," produced by Acid Wizard.

These devs wanted to counter the gray-market key resellers, and they wanted their game to reach as many people as possible. So, they posted a torrent of the complete game to Pirate Bay. It's exactly the same game as the one purchased for retail; no pirate hats or anything. They ask that, if you download the torrent and enjoy the game, to please purchase a copy from wherever it is sold (Steam and GOG, at least).

When the big corporate devs become money-grubbing whores, it's awesome to see a tiny little studio (Acid Wizard is three guys from Poland) eschew the profit motive for the sake of getting people to play their game.

The game itself is a 2-D, top-down survival horror game with no jump scares. It relies on sound, atmosphere, and art style to create its mood, and it's quite effective and well-crafted, IMHO. It's also, as the game states at the outset, a "challenging and unforgiving game." Well worth the $20US they're charging. They deserve all the support they can get.
